# 1.2.65 - what the chat tells whom

The ninth stage on the way to 1.3.0. Foundry sends every chat card, and every
roll's document, to every browser, where a console reads it whatever the Chat
tab shows. 1.2.65 decides, card by card and roll by roll, what reaches whose
browser: a roll the module throws names nobody, a private card's facts travel
with its words, the GMs' prose stays the GMs', and while an incident runs the
cards and dice of the fight reach its own side and nobody else. The chat log
written before 1.2.65 is rewritten on the first load to read the same way.

## Before installing

1. **Copy the world** (Foundry's backup of the world in Setup, or a copy of the
   world's folder). The first load rewrites the chat log written before 1.2.65,
   and a copy is the only way back to it.
2. **After the first load as the primary GM, Back up the case** (GM panel,
   Between sessions). The file now holds the Confusions waiting to be rolled;
   keep it where no player can open it.

## The migration

A moment after the first load of 1.2.65, the primary GM's browser runs four
steps, once:

- **The old chat log, rewritten as today's cards.** The module's old rolls and
  private cards are written as they are written today: what is veiled now is
  veiled (a trap's receipt, a reshape card, Confusion's cards, a Loaded Die's
  notice, a worn or broken tool, a Hope Call's receipt, the time of day told
  during an incident), a roll's list loses an incident's other players, and a
  ruling that was not settled keeps its buttons.
- **Armed Calls unsigned**: a Call armed before the upgrade no longer names who
  bought it.
- **Open repairs of secret projects sealed**: named "Repair" and sealed to
  whoever can see what they repair.
- **Confusions moved into the GMs' store**: a Confusion armed and not yet rolled
  leaves its target's sheet data for the GMs' browsers and its target's
  player's.

Each step reads back what it wrote. A step that did not change what it should
have leaves the world as it was and a notice that stays on screen ("the data
migration stopped short"), and the next load of the world tries again. How many
old cards a played world holds, and how long the rewrite takes on one, was not
measured.

## Do not go back to 1.2.64

Read in the code, not tried on a 1.2.64 build. The rewrite of the old chat log
is not undone. A 1.2.64 build finds a roll's character on the roll's document,
which names nobody for a roll 1.2.65 threw or rewrote: its Despair award, its
Reroll and the diagnostics find no character there. A Confusion waiting to be
rolled is in the GMs' store, where 1.2.64 does not look, so it is lost.

## Changed

- **A roll the module throws names nobody** on its document - no speaker, no
  title, no actor, no statistic's name - and is whispered to the GMs alone, its
  roller reading their own. The Despair award, the Reroll and the diagnostics
  take its character from the GMs' record, reported by whoever threw it.
- **Dice only where the rule says.** The 3D dice of a private roll are shown to
  its roller and the GMs, and in an incident's fight to its participants, and
  so are a Reroll's. A roll nobody on a browser can read
  no longer lights that browser's Chat tab.
- **An incident's cards to its own side.** One table decides who is in an
  incident. A direct murder's victim is told only once it starts, and the
  opening roll's result goes to its own side: a failed opening leaves the victim
  nothing, a successful one tells the victim everything at once. Each holder of
  the incident's record is sent their own copy; a trap's builder reaches only
  the killers.
- **While an incident runs, every private card that names somebody is veiled**,
  whoever posts it and whoever it is about: it speaks as Monokuma, names nobody,
  and a browser that was not sent its words never shows it.
- **A private card's own facts travel with its words**, and a player's copy of
  a ruling card carries no GM-only line and no GM button.
- **The trap's receipt and the reshape card** are in the killer's and the GMs'
  messenger thread, veiled everywhere else; the Plant button on the receipt
  still plants.
- **The safeword's card is posted by a GM's browser.** When no GM's browser
  answers within three seconds (none connected, or one reloading), the player's
  own browser posts it, and the player's card says so. The siren sounds only for
  the safeword's own card.
- **A hidden stash's -1 lands on the total after the roll**, not as a
  disadvantage die in the roll window: the window no longer tells a player that
  somebody hid something in the room. The card says so, the GM's card for
  "something specific" carries the same line, and a Reroll scores its new dice
  with it.
- **A Confusion's armed Call is the GMs' and its target's player's**, not a
  flag on the target's sheet. A season reset that clears action budgets clears
  waiting Confusions with them.
- **Secret projects and traps**: a secret project's repair is sealed and named
  "Repair", and its end is a veiled card; a watched sabotage of a secret project
  or a trap tells the room "a project"; the plant reply carries the item alone,
  not the trap's project. A trap's betrayal is offered to its accomplice
  only, and the betrayal button is on the GM's own after-incident screen.
- **Rooms not found stay unnamed**: a refused crossing and the Rest window name
  only the rooms the character has found.
- **The GMs' reports go to the GM who asked**: the music report, the season
  checklist, the voice plan and the anonymity audit are private cards to that
  GM.

## Known gaps

- Who created a roll or a card stays on its document: a roll a player throws
  names that player, in an incident too (a later release).
- That a veiled card exists, and when it was posted, is on every browser.
- A roll's formula carries the statistic's value.
- Daggerheart's own reroll from a plain sheet roll's card throws its 3D dice on
  every screen.
- A roll the module did not throw keeps Daggerheart's card and its speaker,
  whispered to the GMs and that character's player.
- A Reroll's dice are still sent to every browser.
- The first load leaves in the chat log what it cannot rewrite without taking
  words from a reader: whispers that carry their words in the document (the
  module's older ones and every whisper that is not the module's), 1.2.64's
  public card for the end of a secret project's repair, an old card of a veiled
  kind known only by its words when the primary GM's browser does not hold
  them, and a Monocub's roll's list. Clearing the chat log at a case's end
  removes them.
- 1.2.64's other fight cards (an item used, a Call armed on a participant) are
  not rewritten: an old card does not record that an incident was running.
- An old veiled thread card keeps its place in its thread only on the browsers
  connected at the first load.
- A safeword posted by the player's own browser names the caller in its record,
  and a GM whose browser was still loading pauses the game by hand.
- A Confusion's critical still shows in its target's actions.

## Checked

- The headless suite: 489 passed, 0 failed, 17 skipped, 0 red. New in the
  suite: R201 to R204. The known leak S04-02 (a bystander's browser held the
  killer's opening roll, naming the killer) closes with this release; what is
  left of it, the author Foundry stamps on a player's roll, is the known leak
  "roll-author", for a later stage. The scenarios end green:
  13-murder-signals 47/47, the security scenario 99/99, 40-flow 55/55,
  61-gmstore-case 85/85, and 72-canary 82/85 and 11-killer-secrecy 12/13, their
  reds each a later stage's or a Foundry limit.
- An independent review in two rounds (security, and whether the change is
  correct and its tests measure); its findings were fixed in nine commits, and
  what they left open is listed above as a known gap.
- Not checked in a real Foundry yet, and listed in the audit's live checks
  (LIVE-E06-01 to 08): the opening through the victim's eyes, a module roll's
  document in a bystander's console on Daggerheart 2.6.5 and 2.10.x, Dice So
  Nice on every account, the Chat tab's pip and sound, the safeword card under
  Daggerheart's template and with a GM reloading, the trap's receipt and the
  reshape card in the messenger, the old cards' rewrite on a copy of a played
  world, and a ruling card on a player's Chat tab. The local release gate needs
  a local Foundry v14 and did not run for this release.
